title: A power multiple of every formal glueing chart section lifts to H^0
statement: Let $R,S$ be commutative rings, $\varphi:R\to S$ flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], $f:\{1,\ldots,t\}\to R$, and $X$ a formal glueing datum [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]. Let $H^0(X)$ be its compatible-section submodule [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-H0], and $M_i$ its $R_{f_i}$-module chart [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. For each index $i$ and $x\in M_i$, there exist $n\geq0$ and $h\in H^0(X)$ such that the $i$-th chart coordinate of $h$ equals $f_i^n x$.

source.place: Remark 05EL; Lemmas 05EQ and 05EP, used in Proposition 05ER, second paragraph (verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05ER and the linked tags 05EL, 05EQ, 05EP).

proof.text: Put $u=f_i$. For $x\in M_i$ construct a localized tuple $e(x)$. Its $M'$-coordinate is $y'=\alpha_i^{-1}(x\otimes1)\in(M')_u$; its $M_j$-coordinate is $y_j=\alpha_{ij}(x/1)\in(M_j)_u$ for every $j$. These expressions are meaningful because $u=f_i$ is invertible on $M_i$, $M_i\otimes_RS$, and $(M_j)_u$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away], [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data]. The cocycle condition (b) with all three indices $i$ says $\alpha_{ii}^2=\alpha_{ii}$ after the canonical iterated-localization identifications; since $\alpha_{ii}$ is an isomorphism, it is the identity. Hence $y_i=x/1$, identified with $x$ under $(M_i)_u\cong M_i$. The tuple $e(x)$ is $R$-linear in $x$.

source.place: Lemma 05EP (lemma-equivalence-I-unit), proof: after a generator becomes a unit one component recovers the others; Remark 05EL, cocycle condition (b)

proof.text: The tuple $e(x)$ satisfies the equations defining H^0 after localization at u. For the $j$th equation, localize condition (a) of [def-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-data] at $u=f_i$ and evaluate it on $y'/1\in((M')_{f_i})_{f_j}$. Its left side, $(\alpha_{ij}\otimes_RS)c^{M_i}_{f_j}(\alpha_i)_{f_j}(y'/1)$, is $\alpha_{ij}(x/1)\otimes1=y_j\otimes1$; its right side, $c^{M_j}_{f_i}(\alpha_j)_{f_i}\sigma^{M'}_{f_i,f_j}(y'/1)$, is the image of $\alpha_j(y')$ under the tensor-localization identification. Hence the $j$th localized equation holds [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-maps] (2), (3). For the $(j,k)$th equation, evaluate condition (b) on $(x/1)/1$ in $((M_i)_{f_j})_{f_k}$ and localize at $u$: its left side is $\alpha_{jk}(y_j/1)$ and its right side is $y_k/1$ after the swaps $\sigma$ identify the iterated localizations [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-canonical-maps] (2). The resulting tuple is compatible in the localized ambient product.

source.place: Remark 05EL (remark-glueing-data), conditions (a) and (b); Lemma 05EP (lemma-equivalence-I-unit); proof of Proposition 05ER (proposition-equivalence), second paragraph

proof.text: There are finitely many prime and chart coordinates. Choose one common denominator f_i^a for the localized tuple by taking the maximum of its exponents. The finitely many prime/chart and overlap compatibility differences of its numerator vanish after localization, so each is killed by a power of f_i. Choose b at least as large as all those exponents and multiply the numerator by f_i^b. The resulting tuple h lies in H^0. In the localized i-th chart its coordinate equals f_i^{a+b} x. Since f_i is a unit on M_i, its map to its own localization is injective, so already p_i(h)=f_i^{a+b} x. Take n=a+b. For f_i=0 the chart module is zero; for t=0 there is no index i; zero rings and zero modules are included.

source.place: Remark 05EL; Lemmas 05EQ and 05EP, used in Proposition 05ER, second paragraph (verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05ER and the linked tags 05EL, 05EQ, 05EP).

proof_origin.place: Expanded numerator form of the localized inverse-tuple construction in steps 2–4 of lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-H0-localization. Stacks 05EQ omits the finite denominator calculation; the calculation is explicitly supplied here.

lean.statement:
theorem h0_chart_power_lift {t : ℕ} (φ : R →+* S) (hflat : φ.Flat)
    (f : Fin t → R) (X : Data.{u, v, w} φ f) (i : Fin t)
    (x : piece (f i) (X.M i)) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (h : h0 φ f X), h.val.2 i = (f i) ^ n • x
